title: FlClash AI routing and DNS privacy: a practical guide
x_thread: A fixed AI IP does not prove the whole connection is private. HTTPS, DNS, WebRTC and IPv6 can take different paths. We wrote a practical FlClash guide that checks each one separately.
Keep normal website routing intact. Give known AI domains a fixed exit, add an optional HK upstream, and keep subscription updates. Avoid an automatic DIRECT fallback in the AI group.
Use encrypted DNS with an explicit proxy path. Keep bootstrap resolution independent of the chain it must resolve. Test DNS separately from the public HTTPS address.
A network test should distinguish a fixed IP from a verified residential connection. A browser risk score cannot establish Claude account status or a calibrated ban probability.
The portable agent Skill previews a local configuration change before applying it. Preserve unrelated rules and credentials, then verify fresh connections. No promise of zero interruption.

3. WebRTC, IPv6 and new HTTPS connections get their own tests.

It includes direct and optional HK upstream configurations, detailed computer settings, and a portable agent Skill that previews changes before applying them. Static and residential are different claims; a browser risk score is not an account-safety guarantee.
